findings.title: SEP-45 client_domain fetch is requester-controlled (SSRF), with HTTP fallback

failing_checks.title: Atomic budget accounting
failing_checks.reason: The balance check reads pending payments with a plain SELECT inside a transaction. It takes no lock and the check is not atomic with the insert, so concurrent requests can both pass. The overcommitted payments then fail at submission with insufficient funds. The result is failed or delayed payments,

failing_checks.title: Externally supplied transactions
failing_checks.reason: Only the host function type is checked. The contract, function, arguments and auth credentials are not inspected before the operation is queued for signing with the distribution account as source.

failing_checks.title: Outbound requests and file paths
failing_checks.reason: The server fetches stellar.toml from a client_domain taken from the challenge, which the requester supplies. The only SSRF protection could be the injected HTTPClient, and it is not shown. AllowHTTPRetry also permits plain HTTP fallback.

failing_checks.title: Verification of incoming authentication
failing_checks.reason: With medium threshold 0 and no client signature, the check passes.

failing_checks.title: Controls outside the prompt
failing_checks.reason: The only control on sponsored operations is the host function type. Contract, function and arguments are not allowlisted, and the distribution account is set as the operation source.
